newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich office looks at campaign fund to pay fine.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich office looks at campaign fund to pay fine.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich's office said Saturday that no decision had been made on whether Gingrich would use campaign funds or his own savings to pay a $300,000 penalty for his admitted breaches of House rules.

Asked where the sum would come from, a Gingrich spokeswoman said: "That decision has not been made." But she referred to what she called a House ethics committee-approved precedent for using campaign funds to pay a fine.

She cited the 1994 ethics case against Representative Martin Frost, a Texas Democrat. Frost was directed by the ethics committee to reimburse the U.S. Treasury for inappropriately using an official staff aide for activities in his district.

"He did so, and that time he used campaign contributions for that purpose," the spokeswoman, Lauren Maddox, said in a telephone interview. The office of the House historian was not immediately available to provide details of the Frost penalty.

Maddox said she had not spoken directly to Gingrich "and I am not sure how that money will be reimbursed or from where." Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, is second in the line of succession to become president under the Constitution after Vice President Al Gore.

The ethics committee voted 7-1 on Friday night to recommend that he be reprimanded and required to pay $300,000 after concluding that his use of tax-deductible money for political purposes and inaccurate information supplied to investigators amounted to "intentional or ... reckless" disregard of House rules.
The full House votes on the penalty on Tuesday.
